newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest milling wheat up on market sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Budapest milling wheat up on market sentiment.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange went limit-up on Monday, driven by one brokerage, but fundamentals did not justify the rise, traders said.
"There was no trading in Chicago on Friday to give any direction so the rise was due to market sentiment rather than hard news," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap brokerage.
Milling wheat prices finished the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne higher for all maturities, with August ending at 20,400 forints, December at 21,400 and May at 23,800.
Uzonyi added that the rise was also partly due to the closing of positions.
He said stormy weather over the weekend had had little effect on wheat prices.

Attila Bussay of the National Meteorological Service (OMSZ) said winds close to 100 km per hour combined with rainfall of 50 mm in some places could delay wheat harvesting, but the rains had also dispelled fears of a drought.
Maize prices were mostly trendless in moderate turnover, with significant movements for only two maturities.
March dropped 350 forints to 20,050 and May went limit-down to 21,200 forints.
"Some new positions have been opened for those maturities and the market felt lower prices were in order," he said.
Total grains turnover remained a modest 674 lots or 270 million forints, similar to Friday's 708 lots or 280 million forints.
